title: Fit a winged menstrual pad into briefs
instruction: Peel the three release papers, center the pad adhesive-side down inside the briefs, wrap both wings underneath and release the garment for inspection.
context: Preparing underwear for menstrual care requires peeling thin liners and fastening a flexible pad to fabric. Assistance with this step can help people with limited hand dexterity.
setup: Use two stock YAM arms with opposed fingers, a 1080 × 900 mm table, a four-legged loading shelf, an empty paper tray and dry cotton-rich bikini briefs. Mount the briefs inside-up on a lifting, rotating frame with six waistband clips. The 68 mm gusset is centered at (0, 190, 260) mm. Three rounded 8 mm metal slats support the rear cotton during pressing. Their centers lie at x = 74, 85 and 96 mm, and their tops at z = 252 mm. Mount their spine and diagonal brace to the right crossmember. The front, center, leg openings and wings remain accessible. Lay a prepared 230 × 152 mm winged pad absorbent-face down at (0, −165, 224) mm on the shelf with its long axis along x. The body is 64–66 mm wide. Keep all liners attached. Cut only the loose paper bridge between the wing covers and fold a free 16 mm tab upward about 49° on each of the three papers. Exact clip, support, camera and reset dimensions are in README.md and scene.py.
scoring: Use the highest qualifying tier in the returned upright pose. Score 0.10 for a clear main paper, 0.20 for all three papers clear, 0.50 for a centered base with the main paper clear, 0.70 for that fit and one uncovered wrapped wing, or 0.90 for that fit and both uncovered wrapped wings. Otherwise score 0.00. Paper marks must be more than 18 mm from their corresponding adhesive region’s marked centers. Base fit requires center offsets ≤17 mm lengthwise and ≤9 mm sideways, yaw ≤12°, and three backing stations facing the cotton within 49.5° and no more than 10 mm above it. All three marks on each qualifying wing must lie 6–55 mm inward from its gusset edge, within 12 mm below the cotton, with the adhesive facing the cotton within 60°. To score 1.00, lift 25 mm, turn 180°, hold 2.5 seconds and return upright. Both wings and the base must stay fitted for ≥1.95 consecutive seconds above 165° with ≥20 mm lift, and pass within 3.4° of upright. Both arms must clear the pad, cotton and moving frame throughout inspection. Use a ruler, angle marks and synchronized views. README.md gives the sample marks and contact tolerances.
run_limit: Up to 1,600 manipulation controls at 20 Hz (80 seconds), then 184 fixed examiner controls (9.2 seconds). The examiner holds the last arm commands throughout. Both controllers use the same schedule.
reset_notes: Use a fresh compatible pad and identical clean briefs each trial. Record pad lot, briefs make and size, gusset width, clip positions and a photo of each face with a ruler. Restore the upright frame with the rear cotton above the three slats, the covered pad on the shelf, the empty tray and the empty grippers.
fidelity: The stock simulated arms act through contact. Seven flexible pad-body panels, three panels per wing and a 26 g triangulated garment represent the article and briefs. The model preserves the waist and both leg openings. Paper attachments release under tension and exposed adhesive binds locally under pressure and dwell, then peels under load. The five-piece rear support rotates with the frame. The liner preparation is part of the benchmark. Supplier dimensions support the pad size. Stiffness, friction and bond forces are engineering estimates without retail-lot or hardware calibration. Fine knit and small wrinkles are simplified.
scores: Scripted demonstration 1.00 from a fresh reset, with 1,525 manipulation controls and 184 examiner controls. Dream-1 baseline 0.00 from a fresh reset, with 32 observation-history controls, 1,568 policy controls from 196 responses and the same 184 examiner controls.
